fatal_errors: The proposed Q235 cold-rolling/stress-relief system does not reconstruct the target system of an AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L followed by annealing.
The exposure conditions differ fundamentally: 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature and 60 °C replaces 3.5 wt% H2SO4 electrochemistry and 900 °C molten-salt hot corrosion.

The cited evidence concerns HEAs, additively manufactured material, or cold-rolled alloys rather than direct measurements on Q235 steel; E1 establishes retained dislocations and work hardening but not their effect on corrosion.

Stress-relief annealing may change recovery, texture, carbide state, oxide condition, and surface chemistry in addition to residual stress, so the design does not fully isolate the claimed governing mediator.
explanation: The hypothesis answers the literal Q235-oriented prompt well: it specifies a testable intervention, untreated control, two temperatures, mediator measurements, predicted corrosion behavior, boundaries, uncertainty, and a clear falsification rule. The three-arm design is reasonably discriminating, although an annealing-only control and matched surface preparation would be needed to separate stress relief from thermal and surface-state effects. Scientifically, residual tensile stress and deformation defects could promote dissolution or corrosion localization, but the evidence supplied is indirect and largely drawn from materially different HEA and additive-manufacturing systems. Carbon steel in aerated chloride solution may also undergo substantial general corrosion rather than the passive-film-controlled pitting behavior assumed. Relative to the hidden target, there is essentially no reconstruction of the material, coating intervention, annealing optimum, corrosion media, passive-oxide mechanism, or reported outcomes. It is therefore a plausible but weakly evidenced alternative rather than a partial reconstruction.
